meeting.title: Northstar private pilot readiness
meeting.purpose: Define what ready by month-end means and align five execution functions around one private-pilot milestone.

evidence.text: August 31 means private-pilot readiness for five selected customers, not public launch.
Pilot scope is invite, brief, and review; analytics and SSO are deferred.
Design acceptance uses clear hierarchy, restrained color and motion, plus empty, loading, and error states.
Marketing prepares only a pilot onboarding email and one-page overview; no public campaign or broad announcement.
Sales selects five existing customers with workflow fit and weekly-feedback agreement, without pricing or production-readiness promises.
Production pilot access depends on a security review.
Security review owner, scope, date, and data-retention requirements are unresolved.
Pilot support response time and Engineering escalation path are unresolved.
Weekly feedback collection, synthesis ownership, and format are unresolved.
Maya will obtain a security-review owner, scope, and review date from Operations by 6 p.m. on the meeting date.
Product will publish the frozen scope and acceptance list by August 20.
Engineering will deliver the tested core flow in staging by August 28.
Design will complete core states by August 24 and review them with Product on August 26.
Product supplies approved pilot wording by August 27; Marketing delivers two pilot materials by August 29.
Sales delivers the five-customer list by August 22.
Product will bring a support and feedback operating proposal to the August 26 review.
Public launch, production-readiness claims, and pricing promises are outside the milestone.
Analytics and SSO are deferred beyond the August milestone.

decisions.statement: August 31 means private-pilot readiness for five selected customers, not public launch.
Pilot scope is invite, brief, and review; analytics and SSO are deferred.
Design acceptance covers hierarchy, restrained color and motion, and all core states.
Sales selects five suitable existing customers and makes no pricing or production-readiness promise.

rejected_or_deferred.statement: Public launch, production-readiness claims, and pricing promises are rejected for this milestone.

open_questions.statement: Who owns the security review, what is its scope, when will it occur, and what data-retention rule applies?
What support response time and Engineering escalation path will apply?
Who owns weekly feedback collection and synthesis, and what format will be used?

actions.action: Publish frozen scope and acceptance list.
actions.definition_of_done: Each core step names the user action, expected response, and sign-off owner.

actions.action: Name the security-review owner, scope, and review date.

actions.definition_of_done: Happy, empty, loading, and error states meet the three confirmed design criteria.

actions.action: Run and record the design acceptance review.
actions.definition_of_done: Every state is approved or has a named issue owner and due date.

actions.action: Deliver the tested core flow in staging.
actions.definition_of_done: Invite, brief, and review complete on the supported browser and automated core-flow tests pass.
Copy states the three-step scope and labels analytics and SSO unavailable.

actions.action: Deliver the pilot onboarding email and one-page overview.
actions.definition_of_done: Links work, copy matches Product's approved scope, and Maya approves the wording.
Each record includes workflow fit, main contact, and weekly-feedback confirmation.

actions.action: Propose the support and feedback operating model.
actions.definition_of_done: Proposal names support response time, Engineering escalation, feedback owner, and feedback format.

alignment_gaps.phrase: Production pilot access still depends on a security review.
alignment_gaps.what_is_known: Security approval is required before production pilot access.
alignment_gaps.what_is_missing: Owner, scope, review date, and acceptance outcome.

alignment_gaps.phrase: We still need a decision on data retention for pilot briefs.
alignment_gaps.what_is_known: The question belongs inside the security review.
alignment_gaps.what_is_missing: Policy owner, retention period, deletion behavior, and customer wording.

alignment_gaps.what_is_known: Product will propose an operating model on August 26.
alignment_gaps.what_is_missing: Contact, response time, severity definition, and Engineering escalation.

alignment_gaps.phrase: Who collects the weekly customer feedback?
alignment_gaps.what_is_known: Selected customers must agree to weekly feedback.
alignment_gaps.what_is_missing: Collection owner, synthesis owner, format, cadence, and decision-use path.

understanding_checks.statement: I own the frozen scope, acceptance record, approved pilot wording, and support/feedback proposal by the stated dates; done means the shared pilot boundary and every acceptance field are explicit.

I own the tested invite-brief-review flow in staging by August 28; done means the supported-browser flow completes and automated core-flow tests pass, while pilot access remains dependent on security.
I own all core-flow states by August 24 and the joint review on August 26; done means every state meets the three design criteria or has a named issue owner and date.
I own the pilot onboarding email and one-page overview by August 29; done means links work, copy matches Product's approved scope, and Maya approves the wording.
I own the five-customer list by August 22; done means each customer fits the workflow, has a contact, and agrees to weekly feedback, with no pricing or production-readiness promise.

alignment_score.disclaimer: This score describes clarity in this meeting record. It is not a scientific measure of people or organizational performance.

limitations: The transcript and every participant are fictional.
Security, data retention, support escalation, and feedback ownership remain unresolved by design.
No customer contact, task-system update, or other external action is authorized.
The Alignment Score is explanatory and not a people or performance metric.
